chapters.title: Vairagya Prakarana — The Arising of Dispassion

verses.sanskrit: जगज्जालं मनोजालं मनः संसारकारणम् | तन्मनः शोधयाम्यद्य बोधेन परमात्मनः ||
verses.transliteration: jagajjālaṃ manojālaṃ manaḥ saṃsārakāraṇam | tanmanaḥ śodhayāmyadya bodhena paramātmanaḥ ||
verses.translation: The web of the world is the web of the mind — the mind is the cause of samsara. That mind I purify today through the knowledge of the supreme Self.
verses.hindi: जगत् का जाल मन का जाल है — मन ही संसार का कारण है। उस मन को मैं आज परमात्मा के बोध से शुद्ध करता हूँ।
verses.commentary: "Jagajjālaṃ manojālaṃ" — the web of the world is the web of the mind. The world-as-experienced is identical to the mind's own projections. The web catches because we take it for something external and independent. "Manaḥ saṃsārakāraṇam" — the mind, by its habitual structures of desire and aversion, creates the experience of bondage. Solution: "bodhena paramātmanaḥ" — not repression of the mind but its illumination through knowledge of the Self.
verses.wordMeaning: "Jagajjālaṃ manojālaṃ" — the web of the world is the web of the mind. The world-as-experienced is identical to the mind's own projections. The web catches because we take it for something external and independent. "Manaḥ saṃsārakāraṇam" — the mind, by its habitual structures of desire and aversion, creates the experience of bondage. Solution: "bodhena paramātmanaḥ" — not repression of the mind but its illumination through knowledge of the Self.

verses.sanskrit: न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति | हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते ||
verses.transliteration: na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati | haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate ||
verses.translation: Desire is never extinguished by the enjoyment of desired objects — just as fire fed with ghee only burns higher.
verses.hindi: कामना कभी भोग से शांत नहीं होती — जैसे घी डालने से अग्नि और बढ़ती है।
verses.commentary: The fundamental structure of desire is self-perpetuating. Every satisfied desire generates a new desire — larger, more intense. "Haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva" — like fire fed with ghee. The Yoga Vasistha does not say do not enjoy — it says: do not expect enjoyment to produce the fulfilment it promises. This recognition clears the ground for a satisfaction that does not depend on circumstances.
verses.wordMeaning: The fundamental structure of desire is self-perpetuating. Every satisfied desire generates a new desire — larger, more intense. "Haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva" — like fire fed with ghee. The Yoga Vasistha does not say do not enjoy — it says: do not expect enjoyment to produce the fulfilment it promises. This recognition clears the ground for a satisfaction that does not depend on circumstances.

verses.sanskrit: विवेकः प्रथमं साधनं वैराग्यं द्वितीयं स्मृतम् | षट्सम्पत्तिस्तृतीयं च मुमुक्षुत्वं चतुर्थकम् ||
verses.transliteration: vivekaḥ prathamaṃ sādhanaṃ vairāgyaṃ dvitīyaṃ smṛtam | ṣaṭsampattiḥ tṛtīyaṃ ca mumukṣutvaṃ caturtham ||
verses.translation: Viveka is the first qualification; Vairagya the second; Shatsampatti the third; Mumukshutva the fourth.
verses.hindi: विवेक पहला साधन; वैराग्य दूसरा; षट्सम्पत्ति तीसरी; और मुमुक्षुत्व चौथा।
verses.commentary: Viveka: capacity to distinguish the permanent from impermanent — consciousness alone is constant. Vairagya: withdrawal of the conviction that worldly objects provide permanent satisfaction. Shatsampati: six disciplines (shama, dama, uparati, titiksha, shraddha, samadhana) that bring the mind to stable, alert quietness. Mumukshutva: genuine burning desire for freedom — not luxury but necessity. Without this desire, the teaching produces only intellectual entertainment.
verses.wordMeaning: Viveka: capacity to distinguish the permanent from impermanent — consciousness alone is constant. Vairagya: withdrawal of the conviction that worldly objects provide permanent satisfaction. Shatsampati: six disciplines (shama, dama, uparati, titiksha, shraddha, samadhana) that bring the mind to stable, alert quietness. Mumukshutva: genuine burning desire for freedom — not luxury but necessity. Without this desire, the teaching produces only intellectual entertainment.

chapters.title: Utpatti Prakarana — Consciousness Projecting the World

verses.sanskrit: सर्गादौ सर्गमध्ये च सर्गान्ते च महामते | चिन्मात्रमेव विद्यते नान्यत्किञ्चिदपि स्थितम् ||
verses.transliteration: sargādau sargamadhye ca sargānte ca mahāmate | cinmātrameva vidyate nānyatkiñcidapi sthitam ||
verses.translation: At the beginning, middle, and end of creation, O great-minded one — consciousness alone exists. Nothing else whatsoever stands.
verses.hindi: हे महामते! सृष्टि के आदि, मध्य और अंत में — चिन्मात्र ही विद्यमान है। इससे अलग कुछ भी स्थित नहीं।
verses.commentary: "Cinmātrameva vidyate" — consciousness alone exists, without remainder, at every stage of cosmic time. This removes the possibility of a pre-conscious primordial matter from which consciousness later emerges — the standard materialist story. The Yoga Vasistha reverses this: consciousness is primary; matter, time, and space are its appearances. "Nānyatkiñcidapi sthitam" — nothing else whatsoever stands.
verses.wordMeaning: "Cinmātrameva vidyate" — consciousness alone exists, without remainder, at every stage of cosmic time. This removes the possibility of a pre-conscious primordial matter from which consciousness later emerges — the standard materialist story. The Yoga Vasistha reverses this: consciousness is primary; matter, time, and space are its appearances. "Nānyatkiñcidapi sthitam" — nothing else whatsoever stands.

chapters.title: Upashama Prakarana — The Dissolution of Vasanas

verses.sanskrit: वासनैव हि संसारो वासनाक्षयमुक्तिदम् | तस्माद्वासनया शुद्ध्या संसारविनिवर्तनम् ||
verses.transliteration: vāsanaiva hi saṃsāro vāsanākṣayamuktidaṃ | tasmādvāsanayā śuddhyā saṃsāravinivarttanam ||
verses.translation: Vasana alone is samsara. The destruction of vasana is liberation. Therefore, through the purification of vasana comes the cessation of samsara.
verses.hindi: वासना ही संसार है। वासनाक्षय ही मुक्ति है। इसलिए वासना की शुद्धि से संसार की निवृत्ति होती है।
verses.commentary: "Vāsanaiva hi saṃsāraḥ" — vasana alone is samsara. Not the world itself but the habitual patterns of desire, aversion, and identification that structure experience. The world appears as bondage only because it is experienced through the lens of accumulated vasanas. "Vāsanākṣayamuktidaṃ" — the destruction of vasana is liberation. Not a different world, not a different body — the same world, experienced without the vasana-lens, is liberation. This is why jivan-mukti is possible: liberation in the body, while living, because the bondage was never in the world but in the vasanas.
verses.wordMeaning: "Vāsanaiva hi saṃsāraḥ" — vasana alone is samsara. Not the world itself but the habitual patterns of desire, aversion, and identification that structure experience. The world appears as bondage only because it is experienced through the lens of accumulated vasanas. "Vāsanākṣayamuktidaṃ" — the destruction of vasana is liberation. Not a different world, not a different body — the same world, experienced without the vasana-lens, is liberation. This is why jivan-mukti is possible: liberation in the body, while living, because the bondage was never in the world but in the vasanas.

chapters.title: Nirvana Prakarana — Jivan-Mukti: Liberation While Living

verses.sanskrit: जीवन्मुक्तः स विज्ञेयो बद्धमुक्ताभिमानवान् | यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ||
verses.transliteration: jīvanmuktaḥ sa vijñeyo baddhamuktābhimānavān | yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati ||
verses.translation: He is to be known as jivan-mukta — free while apparently bound — who neither exults, nor hates, nor grieves, nor desires.
verses.hindi: वह जीवन्मुक्त जाना जाए — बंधे हुए में भी मुक्त — जो न हर्षित होता है, न द्वेष करता है, न शोक करता है, न इच्छा करता है।
verses.commentary: The Yoga Vasistha's portrait of the jivan-mukta — the one liberated in life. The four negatives are not emotional suppression: "na hṛṣyati" — no exultation at gain; "na dveṣṭi" — no hatred of opposition; "na śocati" — no grief at loss; "na kāṅkṣati" — no craving for what is absent. These are not achieved by willpower but by the natural consequence of seeing through the vasana-lens. When the vasanas are dissolved, the automatic emotional reactivity they generate dissolves with them. The jivan-mukta is not cold or detached — they are fully alive, but without the compulsive quality that makes ordinary life feel like bondage.
verses.wordMeaning: The Yoga Vasistha's portrait of the jivan-mukta — the one liberated in life. The four negatives are not emotional suppression: "na hṛṣyati" — no exultation at gain; "na dveṣṭi" — no hatred of opposition; "na śocati" — no grief at loss; "na kāṅkṣati" — no craving for what is absent. These are not achieved by willpower but by the natural consequence of seeing through the vasana-lens. When the vasanas are dissolved, the automatic emotional reactivity they generate dissolves with them. The jivan-mukta is not cold or detached — they are fully alive, but without the compulsive quality that makes ordinary life feel like bondage.

verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो चिन्मात्रसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogaḥ cinmātrasamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on pure consciousness.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग चिन्मात्र पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of pure consciousness. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of pure consciousness (cinmātra).
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of pure consciousness. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of pure consciousness (cinmātra).

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं चिन्मात्र एव सर्वं चिन्मात्र मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ cinmātra eva sarvaṃ cinmātra mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is pure consciousness alone, all is pure consciousness in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब चिन्मात्र ही है, सब चिन्मात्र मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with pure consciousness as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is pure consciousness; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with pure consciousness as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is pure consciousness; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो चिन्मात्रे लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo cinmātre līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into pure consciousness. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव चिन्मात्र में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into pure consciousness. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into pure consciousness. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं चिन्मात्र नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ cinmātra nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual pure consciousness — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत चिन्मात्र — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of pure consciousness: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of pure consciousness: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो चिन्मात्रं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo cinmātraṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows pure consciousness in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो चिन्मात्र को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्मात्र सर्वभूतानां हृदये संनिविष्टा | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: cinmātra sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭā | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Pure consciousness dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: चिन्मात्र सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निवास करती है। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The Yoga Vasistha declares that pure consciousness dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Pure consciousness is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.
verses.wordMeaning: The Yoga Vasistha declares that pure consciousness dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Pure consciousness is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्मात्र प्राणः प्राणेश्चैव चिन्मात्र सर्वेषु भूतेषु | यो चिन्मात्रं प्राणरूपेण जानाति स मुक्तो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: cinmātra prāṇaḥ prāṇeścaiva cinmātra sarveṣu bhūteṣu | yo cinmātraṃ prāṇarūpeṇa jānāti sa mukto bhavati ||
verses.translation: Pure consciousness is prana, pure consciousness is the lord of prana, pure consciousness is in all beings. He who knows pure consciousness as the form of prana becomes liberated.
verses.hindi: चिन्मात्र प्राण हैं, चिन्मात्र प्राणेश हैं, चिन्मात्र सभी प्राणियों में हैं। जो चिन्मात्र को प्राण-रूप में जानता है, वह मुक्त हो जाता है।
verses.commentary: The Yoga Vasistha identifies pure consciousness with prana — the life breath. "Cinmātra prāṇaḥ" — pure consciousness is prana. "Cinmātra prāṇeśaḥ" — pure consciousness is the lord of prana. "Cinmātra sarveṣu bhūteṣu" — pure consciousness is in all beings. The verse then states that knowing pure consciousness as the form of prana leads to liberation. This is the Yoga Vasistha's core teaching: pure consciousness is not a distant deity but the very breath that animates all life. Recognising pure consciousness in the breath is the most direct spiritual practice.
verses.wordMeaning: The Yoga Vasistha identifies pure consciousness with prana — the life breath. "Cinmātra prāṇaḥ" — pure consciousness is prana. "Cinmātra prāṇeśaḥ" — pure consciousness is the lord of prana. "Cinmātra sarveṣu bhūteṣu" — pure consciousness is in all beings. The verse then states that knowing pure consciousness as the form of prana leads to liberation. This is the Yoga Vasistha's core teaching: pure consciousness is not a distant deity but the very breath that animates all life. Recognising pure consciousness in the breath is the most direct spiritual practice.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्मात्र सर्वस्वरूपो चिन्मात्र सर्वगतः सर्वव्यापी | चिन्मात्रं यो जानाति तत्त्वेन स चिन्मात्रः स स्वयं भवति ||
verses.transliteration: cinmātra sarvasvarūpo cinmātra sarvagataḥ sarvavyāpī | cinmātraṃ yo jānāti tattvena sa cinmātraḥ sa svayaṃ bhavati ||
verses.translation: Pure consciousness is the form of all, pure consciousness is everywhere, pure consciousness is all-pervading. He who knows pure consciousness in truth becomes pure consciousness himself.
verses.hindi: चिन्मात्र सभी का स्वरूप है, चिन्मात्र सर्वत्र है, चिन्मात्र सर्वव्यापी है। जो चिन्मात्र को तत्व से जानता है, वह स्वयं चिन्मात्र हो जाता है।
verses.commentary: The Yoga Vasistha declares that pure consciousness is the form of all, everywhere, all-pervading. "Cinmātra sarvasvarūpaḥ" — pure consciousness is the form of all. "Cinmātra sarvagataḥ" — pure consciousness is everywhere. "Cinmātra sarvavyāpī" — pure consciousness is all-pervading. The verse then states that knowing pure consciousness in truth leads to becoming pure consciousness oneself. This is the Yoga Vasistha's ultimate teaching: liberation is the recognition that you are pure consciousness — the awareness that animates all existence. When you know pure consciousness in truth, you become pure consciousness.
verses.wordMeaning: The Yoga Vasistha declares that pure consciousness is the form of all, everywhere, all-pervading. "Cinmātra sarvasvarūpaḥ" — pure consciousness is the form of all. "Cinmātra sarvagataḥ" — pure consciousness is everywhere. "Cinmātra sarvavyāpī" — pure consciousness is all-pervading.
